question: Fill in the blank with the correct conjunction: '_______ he was feeling very tired, he completed his assignment on time.' ✍️
explanation: Awesome! 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction used to introduce a contrasting idea or a concession. He completed it despite being tired! 🌟
hint: You need a word that shows a contrast between being tired and finishing the work.

question: Choose the best conjunction: 'She wanted to buy a new laptop, ______ she started saving a portion of her salary every month.' 💻
explanation: Brilliant! 'So' is a coordinating conjunction used to show the result or consequence of an action. She wanted a laptop, resulting in her saving money! 💸
hint: Look for a word that shows the result or consequence.

question: Which conjunction fits best? 'You can either take the subway ______ book a cab to reach the museum.' 🚇
explanation: Spot on! 'Either...or' is a correlative conjunction pair used to present two alternative choices. 🚕
hint: This word usually pairs up with 'either' to show a choice.

question: Complete the sentence: 'The new student is not only an excellent debater ______ a talented musician.' 🎤
explanation: Excellent! 'Not only... but also' is a correlative conjunction pair used to link two positive attributes about the same subject. 🎶
hint: This pairs with 'not only' to add extra emphasis.

question: Fill in the blank: '_______ you start practicing daily, you will not be able to clear the driving test.' 🚗
explanation: Fantastic! 'Unless' means 'if not' and introduces a condition that must be met to avoid a negative outcome. 🚦
hint: Think of a word that means 'except on the condition that'.

question: Select the correct conjunction: 'I will send you a text message ______ I reach the railway station.' 📱
explanation: Great job! 'As soon as' is a subordinating conjunction of time, showing that one action will happen immediately after another. 🚆
hint: Look for a phrase that means 'immediately when'.

question: Complete the pair: 'Neither the class monitor ______ the students knew about the surprise test.' 📝
explanation: Perfect! 'Neither...nor' is a correlative conjunction pair used to link two negative options or subjects. 🙅‍♂️
hint: This word is the negative partner to 'neither'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'The cafe is famous for its delicious pastries; ______, it is quite expensive for students.' 🍰
explanation: Outstanding! 'However' is a conjunctive adverb used to introduce a contrasting statement. The food is great, but there is a downside! ☕
hint: You need a word that shows contrast, similar to 'but'.

question: Choose the best option: 'Rohan stayed at home all day ______ he was suffering from a severe fever.' 🤒
explanation: Awesome! 'Because' is a subordinating conjunction that introduces the reason or cause for an action. 🏡
hint: This word provides the reason why Rohan stayed home.

question: Complete the sentence: 'No sooner had the principal entered the auditorium ______ the students stopped talking.' 🤫
explanation: Brilliant! The phrase 'no sooner' is always paired with 'than' to indicate that one action happened immediately after another. 🏫
hint: This word pairs specifically with 'no sooner'.

question: Fill in the blank: '______ you apologize for your rude behavior, I will not talk to you.' 😠
explanation: Spot on! 'Until' is used as a subordinating conjunction to show the time up to which a certain condition applies. 🕒
hint: Think of a word that means 'up to the point in time that'.

question: Which conjunction fits best? 'She loves reading mystery novels, ______ her younger brother prefers comic books.' 📖
explanation: Excellent! 'Whereas' is used to highlight a contrast or comparison between two different people or things. 📚
hint: Look for a word that means 'in contrast to'.

question: Complete the sentence: 'I bought some extra flour and sugar ______ I could bake a cake for her birthday.' 🎂
explanation: Fantastic! 'So that' is a subordinating conjunction showing purpose. It explains *why* the extra ingredients were bought. 🎉
hint: This phrase shows the purpose behind the action.

question: Fill in the blank: '______ the weather was extremely stormy, the flight got delayed by three hours.' ✈️
explanation: Perfect! In this context, 'Since' acts as a subordinating conjunction of reason, similar to 'because'. ⛈️
hint: This word introduces the cause of the flight delay.

question: Choose the best option: 'He walked quietly into the room ______ he would not wake up the sleeping baby.' 👶
explanation: Great job! 'So that' is used to express purpose or intention. He walked quietly for the specific purpose of not waking the baby. 🤫
hint: Look for a phrase that explains his intention.

question: Select the correct conjunction: 'We can go to the mountains for our vacation, ______ we can visit the coastal beaches.' 🏖️
explanation: Awesome! 'Or' is a coordinating conjunction used to connect two alternative choices or possibilities. ⛰️
hint: This word connects two different options.

question: Complete the sentence: 'The new smartphone is both highly efficient ______ incredibly affordable.' 📱
explanation: Brilliant! The correlative conjunction 'both' is always paired with 'and' to join two positive traits. 💸
hint: This word pairs perfectly with 'both'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I have been living in this beautiful city ______ I was a little child.' 🌇
explanation: Spot on! 'Since' is used here as a subordinating conjunction of time, indicating the starting point of an ongoing action. 🕒
hint: Think of a word that indicates the starting point in time.

question: Which conjunction fits best? '______ it is a national holiday today, all the banks and post offices are closed.' 🏦
explanation: Excellent! 'As' functions here as a subordinating conjunction of reason, meaning 'because' or 'since'. 🗓️
hint: This word provides the reason why the banks are closed.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Hardly had she stepped out of the building ______ it started raining heavily.' ☔
explanation: Fantastic! The word 'hardly' is a correlative conjunction that always pairs with 'when' to show two events happening in quick succession. 🌧️
hint: This word strictly pairs with 'hardly'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I will definitely attend the farewell party ______ I finish my project on time.' 🎓
explanation: Perfect! 'Provided that' is a subordinating conjunction meaning 'on the condition that'. 📋
hint: Look for a phrase that sets a strict condition.

question: Choose the best option: 'He was completely exhausted from the trip, ______ he refused to go to sleep.' 🧳
explanation: Great job! 'Yet' is a coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS) used to introduce a contrasting but true statement. 🛌
hint: This word acts similar to 'but' to show a surprising contrast.

question: Select the correct conjunction: 'You must submit the application form today; ______, you will have to pay a late fee.' 📝
explanation: Awesome! 'Otherwise' is a conjunctive adverb used to show what will happen if a certain condition is not met. 💸
hint: Think of a word that means 'if not'.

question: Complete the sentence: '______ you work hard and stay focused, you will achieve your dreams.' 🎯
explanation: Brilliant! 'If' is a subordinating conjunction used to introduce a positive condition for success. 🏆
hint: This word introduces a positive condition.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Scarcely had the singer finished her performance ______ the audience erupted in applause.' 🎤
explanation: Spot on! Just like 'hardly', the word 'scarcely' always pairs with 'when' in correlative constructions. 🎶
hint: This word is the traditional pair for 'scarcely'.

question: Which conjunction fits best? 'She speaks French fluently, ______ she lived in Paris for five years during her childhood.' 🇫🇷
explanation: Excellent! As a coordinating conjunction (from FANBOYS), 'for' is used to explain the reason or cause, meaning 'because'. 🗼
hint: Look for a coordinating conjunction that gives a reason.

question: Complete the sentence: 'We waited patiently at the bus stop ______ the bus finally arrived.' 🚏
explanation: Fantastic! 'Until' is a subordinating conjunction showing that the waiting action continued up to a specific point in time. 🚍
hint: This word shows the time up to an event.

question: Fill in the blank: 'Would you prefer to have hot coffee ______ cold iced tea with your sandwich?' 🥪
explanation: Perfect! 'Or' is used here to present a choice between two alternatives. 🥤
hint: You need a word that offers a choice.

question: Choose the best option: 'He was late to the annual meeting ______ there was a massive traffic jam on the highway.' 🚙
explanation: Great job! 'Because' is a subordinating conjunction that clearly introduces the reason for being late. 🚦
hint: This word introduces the cause of his lateness.

question: Select the correct conjunction: '______ it was getting very late, the team continued working on the project.' 🕒
explanation: Awesome! 'Even though' is a subordinating conjunction used to show a strong contrast or concession. They worked *in spite* of the time! 💻
hint: Look for a phrase that means 'despite the fact that'.

question: Complete the sentence: 'Not only did she win the gold medal, ______ she broke the national record.' 🏅
explanation: Brilliant! The correlative conjunction 'not only' must always be paired with 'but also'. 🏃‍♀️
hint: This is the second half of the 'not only' pair.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I really do not know ______ he will accept the job offer or decline it.' 🤷‍♂️
explanation: Spot on! 'Whether' is paired with 'or' to express a choice between two possibilities or alternatives. 💼
hint: This word pairs with 'or' to show two possibilities.

question: Which conjunction fits best? 'She had no other choice ______ to accept the terms of the new contract.' 📄
explanation: Excellent! The phrase 'no other' is followed by the conjunction 'than' to introduce an exception or the only remaining option. 🤝
hint: This word compares the lack of choices to the final option.

question: Complete the sentence: 'The outdoor concert was cancelled ______ the lead guitarist fell terribly ill.' 🎸
explanation: Fantastic! 'Because' is the perfect subordinating conjunction here to explain the reason for the cancellation. 🎤
hint: You need a word that provides the reason.

question: Fill in the blank: 'I will support and follow you ______ you decide to go.' 🚶‍♂️
explanation: Perfect! 'Wherever' is a subordinating conjunction of place, meaning 'in or to whatever place'. 🌍
hint: Look for a word that relates to a place or location.

question: Choose the best option: 'The mathematics teacher was very strict ______ extremely fair with her grading.' 📐
explanation: Great job! 'But' is a coordinating conjunction used to connect two contrasting traits: being strict versus being fair. 👩‍🏫
hint: You need a word that shows contrast between two adjectives.

question: Select the correct conjunction: 'You should always make hay ______ the sun shines.' 🌞
explanation: Awesome! 'While' is a subordinating conjunction indicating that two actions are happening at the same time. It's also a famous idiom! 🌾
hint: Think of a word that means 'during the time that'.

question: Complete the sentence: 'I packed an umbrella in my backpack ______ it rained later in the day.' 🎒
explanation: Brilliant! 'In case' is a conjunction used to talk about things we do to prepare for a possible future situation. 🌧️
hint: Look for a phrase that means 'as a precaution'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'He ran fast ______ he should miss the last train home.' 🏃‍♂️
explanation: Spot on! 'Lest' is a subordinating conjunction that means 'to avoid the risk of' and is traditionally followed by 'should'. 🚆
hint: This is an older conjunction that almost always pairs with 'should'.

question: Which conjunction fits best? '______ had I closed my eyes to sleep than the loud alarm rang.' 🛌
explanation: Excellent! The phrase 'No sooner' is the correct correlative pair for 'than', indicating an immediate sequence of events. 🔔
hint: Look for the phrase that naturally pairs with 'than'.

question: Complete the sentence: 'The car broke down in the middle of nowhere; ______, we managed to reach the venue.' 🚘
explanation: Fantastic! 'Nevertheless' is a conjunctive adverb that means 'in spite of that', showing a strong contrast. 🏁
hint: Think of a word similar to 'however' or 'in spite of that'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'She did not study for the final test, ______ did she complete her practical files.' 📚
explanation: Perfect! 'Nor' is used to connect two negative ideas, continuing the negative sense of 'did not'. 📝
hint: You need a word that adds another negative action.

question: Choose the best option: '______ wealthy he might be, he never donates to charity.' 🏦
explanation: Great job! 'However' used before an adjective means 'no matter how'. It shows that his wealth doesn't change his lack of charity. 🤝
hint: Look for a word that means 'no matter how'.

question: Select the correct conjunction: 'You can borrow my favorite book ______ you promise to return it by tomorrow.' 📖
explanation: Awesome! 'As long as' acts as a subordinating conjunction meaning 'on the condition that'. 🤝
hint: This phrase sets a condition for borrowing the book.

question: Complete the sentence: 'I love watching action movies, ______ my best friend enjoys romantic comedies.' 🍿
explanation: Brilliant! Here, 'while' is used as a subordinating conjunction of contrast, similar to 'whereas', to compare two different tastes. 🎥
hint: You need a word that compares two different preferences.

question: Fill in the blank: '______ the cake was baking in the oven, she prepared the chocolate frosting.' 🧁
explanation: Spot on! 'While' is a subordinating conjunction of time, showing that two actions are happening simultaneously. ⏲️
hint: Think of a word that means 'at the same time as'.

question: Which conjunction fits best? 'He will definitely not join us for dinner ______ we personally invite him.' 🍽️
explanation: Excellent! 'Unless' sets a negative condition, meaning 'except if we personally invite him'. 🍕
hint: Look for a word that sets a strict condition for him to come.

question: Complete the sentence: '______ I heard the shocking news, I rushed immediately to the hospital.' 🚑
explanation: Fantastic! 'As soon as' is a subordinating conjunction of time that highlights an immediate reaction to an event. 🏃‍♂️
hint: This phrase means 'the very moment that'.

question: Fill in the blank: 'They decided to go for a long hike ______ the weather was perfectly clear and sunny.' 🥾
explanation: Perfect! 'As' is used here as a subordinating conjunction of reason, providing the 'why' for their hike. 🌲
hint: You need a short word that gives the reason.

question: Choose the best option: '______ he was born in a very rich family, he lived a simple and humble life.' 🏡
explanation: Great job! 'Though' (or although) introduces a concession or a surprising contrast to the fact that he was rich. ✨
hint: Look for a word that shows a surprising contrast.
